It came in a box with eleven parts, a bag of screws, and instructions drawn by someone who hates me. I watched a man named Gary explain it for forty-five minutes. I paused Gary six times. The chair works now. Mostly. At home, though, my husband still can't find the good scissors without me. The dog still waits by the door at 5:30. My daughter still calls me first when something breaks. The laptop goes in the drawer at six now. The pickles were fine, the pickles are always fine. I stood there in the cold glow with the door wide open, letting all the cold out, exactly the way my father told me never to do.
